clue.text: Consult Ria, discovering about sound waves

indicators.note: discovering is read as uncovering a new arrangement, so the letters of the two names are reworked

explanation.surface: Someone consults a woman called Ria and learns something about acoustics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discovering' signals the anagram of CONSULT RIA; the definition is the closing phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Ultrasonic describes frequencies of vibration above human hearing, a matter of acoustic waves.

clue.text: It is fashionable to raise one's cap in America

parts.note: U, as in 'that is very U', means upper-class and so socially acceptable

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising a word lifts it so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a cap is a kind of hat

explanation.surface: Advice that tipping your hat is the done thing in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raise' turns HAT upwards in this down light to give TAH after U. The definition stands for a place found in America, a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Utah is one of the fifty states of the USA, so it lies within the nation.

clue.text: Sound attempt by Eros to include point, despite it having three points

indicators.note: Sound tells us the following word is to be heard, giving a syllable spelt differently

parts.note: an attempt is a try

indicators.note: to include means the god's name takes in the compass point

parts.note: Eros, the Greek god of love, is Cupid to the Romans
S, south, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A love god's effort at something with one sharp tip, though it really has three.
explanation.walkthrough: TRY said aloud gives TRI; 'to include' puts S inside CUPID to give CUSPID.
explanation.definitionFit: Tricuspid describes a tooth or heart valve with three cusps, or pointed flaps.

clue.text: Bitter result of tossing the caber!

indicators.note: tossing the caber throws it about, so its letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A Highland Games competitor is sour after the caber event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tossing' signals an anagram of CABER. Tossing the caber is a Scottish Highland Games event where a long pole is thrown end over end.
explanation.definitionFit: Acerb is a rare literary adjective for sour or harsh in taste or temper.

clue.text: Former pupil has to wait and see

parts.note: OB, old boy, is a former pupil of a school
to wait at table is to serve

explanation.surface: An old boy of the school has to hang about and see what happens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wait' here is the waiter's job, serving, not hanging about.
explanation.definitionFit: To observe is to notice or watch, a synonym of perceiving with the eyes.

clue.text: I name Hen as one who inserts pages into a text

definitions.text: one who inserts pages into a text

parts.note: a hen kept for eggs is a layer

explanation.surface: Someone designates a chicken as the person who adds pages to a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hen' is a layer, a bird that lays eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: An inlayer is someone who sets material into something else, here extra leaves into a book.

clue.text: Most of the month, nothing more for a Roman goddess

indicators.note: most of a word is all but its last letter, so the month loses its tail

parts.note: June is a month
O, the figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: Most of a month passes with nothing else for a goddess of Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most of' drops the final E of JUNE to give JUN.
explanation.definitionFit: Juno was queen of the gods in Roman myth, wife of Jupiter.

clue.text: Some wasteful travellers in the extreme

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A remark about travellers who waste a great deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Ultra as a prefix or adjective means beyond the usual, excessive.

clue.text: Beyond deputy to be doing what ham is doing

parts.note: over means beyond, as in over the limit
an acting chairman is a deputy standing in

explanation.surface: Going further than a stand-in to behave like a bad actor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ham' is a hammy actor, not the meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A ham actor exaggerates, performing in an overblown theatrical way.

clue.text: Apt article replacing nothing on other side

indicators.note: replacing tells us one letter takes the place of another in the word for the far side

parts.note: opposite means on the other side
O, zero, means nothing
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A suitable item swapped in for an empty space across the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacing' puts A where the first O of OPPOSITE stood.
explanation.definitionFit: Apposite means well suited or relevant to the occasion.

clue.text: Quick drink taken about four

indicators.note: about means the drink goes round the Roman numeral

parts.note: ale is a drink
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone downs a fast drink around four o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quick' has its old sense, living, as in 'the quick and the dead'.
explanation.definitionFit: Quick in its archaic sense means living, as in the quick and the dead.

clue.text: Chemical last produced by man upset at the end

indicators.note: produced is read as made into something new, so the four letters are rearranged
upset means the man's name is knocked into a new order

parts.note: Peter is a man's name

explanation.surface: Something finally made by a man who is distressed at the finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produced' rearranges LAST to SALT; 'upset' turns PETER into PETRE, which comes at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Saltpetre is potassium nitrate, a compound used in gunpowder and curing meat.

clue.text: Fruit, large number, surprisingly blue, right by the railway

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

indicators.note: surprisingly means the colour word turns up in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A list of fruit, lots of it oddly blue, by the railway line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' rearranges BLUE into ULBE.
explanation.definitionFit: A mulberry is a dark berry from a tree of the genus Morus.

clue.text: Order a bit of a laugh in Nebraska

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour
ha is a short burst of laughter

explanation.surface: Someone orders a little humour in a Midwestern state.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition stands for a city found in Nebraska.
explanation.definitionFit: Omaha is the largest city in the US state of Nebraska.

clue.text: Sinuous French one dug round Roman

parts.note: un is French for one

indicators.note: round means the word dug is placed around the language

parts.note: Latin was the Roman language

explanation.surface: A Frenchman excavates around some Roman remains along a winding course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts LATIN inside DUG, between its U and G.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinuous and undulating both describe a wavy, rising-and-falling line.

clue.text: Main god?

parts.note: the main is the sea, so this is the Roman deity ruling the ocean

explanation.definitionFit: The Roman sea god is identified with the Greek Poseidon, ruler of the oceans.

clue.text: Wrongly drawn out, it is not fitting

indicators.note: wrongly means the two words are put together incorrectly, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A picture drawn badly is not suitable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrongly' signals an anagram of DRAWN OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Untoward means improper or unseemly, so unsuitable.

clue.text: Aim to tear about in old clothing

indicators.note: about means the word for a tear goes round the aim

parts.note: a rent is a tear or rip

explanation.surface: Someone plans to rip apart some ancient garments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tear' is a rip, RENT, not crying; 'about' puts it around AIM.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiment is an archaic word for garments or dress.

clue.text: Duck's down for cover

parts.note: the eider is a sea duck
taken as written

explanation.surface: The soft feathers of a duck are used for bedding.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue nearly describes itself: the duck is the eider, whose down fills quilts.
explanation.definitionFit: An eiderdown is a quilt, a bed covering filled with soft feathers.

clue.text: Modernised aloft of old

parts.note: up means aloft
dated means belonging to an earlier time

explanation.surface: Something was brought up to date, from high above and long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: Updated means brought into line with the latest version or fashion.

clue.text: Cease to take part with hippy

definitions.meaning: to withdraw from an activity, as a verb
someone who rejects conventional society, as a noun

explanation.surface: A hippy gives up taking part.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means withdraw from something; as a noun a person who has rejected mainstream society, like a hippy.

clue.text: GP needs break in Germany

parts.note: a GP, general practitioner, is a doctor, abbreviated Dr

indicators.note: break means the word needs is broken up and its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A family doctor requires a holiday in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break' rearranges NEEDS into ESDEN. The definition stands for a city in Germany. GP is the British term for a family doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: Dresden is the capital city of Saxony in eastern Germany.

clue.text: Does family have some woollen cloth?

parts.note: taken as written, the plural of doe, a female deer
kin are family

explanation.surface: A question whether relatives own some woollen material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Does' looks like the verb but is female deer.
explanation.definitionFit: Doeskin is a soft, fine woollen fabric with a napped finish.

clue.text: Early guided missile

parts.note: reads like a first-generation rocket but means an ancient projectile aimed by an archer

explanation.definitionFit: Arrows were among the first projectiles directed at a target, shot from a bow.

clue.text: Alert agile animal

indicators.note: agile suggests nimble movement, so the letters move about into a new order

explanation.surface: A watchful creature that is quick on its feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'agile' signals an anagram of ALERT.
explanation.definitionFit: The ratel is the honey badger, a mammal of Africa and Asia.

clue.text: Peer above another peer

parts.note: over means above
a lord is a peer of the realm

explanation.surface: A nobleman ranks higher than a fellow nobleman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peer' is a lord with others beneath him, not the verb to look.
explanation.definitionFit: An overlord is a supreme ruler, a lord with authority over lesser nobles.

clue.text: One's not successful in the close race

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits inside the words that follow, across the gap

explanation.surface: Someone who failed in a tightly contested contest.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'close race': cLOSE Race.
explanation.definitionFit: A loser is someone who fails to win.

clue.text: Always after two degrees at critical action time

parts.note: D, doctor, is a degree; DD is also Doctor of Divinity
ay, also spelt aye, is an old word for always

explanation.surface: Always following two academic qualifications at a crucial moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places AY after DD.
explanation.definitionFit: D-Day, 6 June 1944, was the Allied invasion of Normandy; the term means a day set for a decisive operation.

clue.text: Cover security device on synchronised mechanism

parts.note: to inter is to bury, covering with earth
a lock is a security device

explanation.surface: A protective lock fitted to a mechanism that works in step.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cover' is to bury, INTER.
explanation.definitionFit: An interlock is a device making parts of a machine operate together in a set sequence.

clue.text: Weapon found on south-west ring-road

parts.note: O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A weapon discovered on a bypass in the south-west.
explanation.definitionFit: A sword is a bladed weapon for cutting and thrusting.

clue.text: Something very precious sportsmen aim for

definitions.meaning: the top medal awarded to a winner

explanation.surface: What athletes chase is highly valuable.
explanation.definitionFit: The yellow metal is prized, and the first-place medal at events like the Olympics is made of it.

clue.text: Practice of wandering from place to place near city in turmoil

definitions.text: Practice of wandering from place to place

indicators.note: turmoil means the words are thrown into confusion, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Roaming about near a city that is in chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turmoil' signals an anagram of NEAR CITY IN; 'in' is part of the fodder, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Itinerancy is the habit of travelling from one place to another, as itinerant workers do.
